predecessors.name: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
predecessors.text: the provinces that signed the Federal Pact of 4 January 1831

successors.name: Argentine Republic
successors.text: the same land: Cliopatria's Argentine Republic row from 1930

ledger.x: 4 January 1831: the Federal Pact founds the Argentine Confederation.
ledger.cpn: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata

ledger.x: 1833: Rosas advances the southern frontier of Buenos Aires province.
1838: Paraguay occupies Misiones.
1840: a further advance of the Buenos Aires frontier (page silent).
11 September 1852: Buenos Aires secedes.
1853: the Confederation's capital moves from Buenos Aires to Parana.
12 December 1861: Buenos Aires returns after Pavon.
December 1861: the Confederation becomes the Republic of Argentina.

1862: the national government returns to Buenos Aires (page silent on the year: the Provinces of Argentina page has only that the city 'was made a federal territory in 1880' and an 1862 law on national territories).
13 April 1865: Paraguay takes Corrientes.
1866: Corrientes is cleared.
1869: Argentine and Brazilian troops occupy Paraguay.
1872: the Territorio Nacional del Gran Chaco.
1876: the Allied occupation of Paraguay ends ('until 1876'; the Machain-Irigoyen Treaty is dated 3 February 1876).
3 February 1876: Paraguay gives up Misiones.
3 February 1876: the Machain-Irigoyen Treaty gives Argentina Misiones and Formosa.
1878: the Hayes award leaves the Chaco Central to Paraguay.
1879: Roca's second sweep takes La Pampa.
1881: Villegas conquers Neuquen.
23 July 1881: Tierra del Fuego is divided with Chile.
23 July 1881: the Andes line fixes Argentine Patagonia.
18 October 1884: the last battle of the Conquest of the Desert.
1899: the Puna de Atacama lawsuit.
1929: Cliopatria's Argentine Confederation row ends and its Argentine Republic row begins in 1930.

wars.name: Rosas's expedition of 1833 (Conquest of the Desert)
wars.outcome: A partial success on the Buenos Aires frontier: 'only Rosas's expedition achieved some success'.

wars.name: Confederation-Buenos Aires war (Cepeda 1859, Pavon 1861)
wars.outcome: Urquiza's Confederation beat Mitre at Cepeda (23 October 1859); Mitre beat Urquiza at Pavon (17 September 1861) and Buenos Aires returned to the Confederation on 12 December 1861, which became the Republic of Argentina.

wars.name: Paraguayan War
wars.outcome: The Triple Alliance won: Solano Lopez died at Cerro Cora on 1 March 1870; Argentine and Brazilian troops occupied Paraguay until 1876 and the Machain-Irigoyen Treaty (3 February 1876) gave Argentina Misiones and Formosa.

wars.name: War of the Peru-Bolivian Confederation
wars.outcome: The Confederation fell at Yungay on 20 January 1839 and was dissolved in 1839.

wars.name: Conquest of the Desert
wars.outcome: Argentina took the Pampas and northern Patagonia: Roca's sweeps of 1878-1879 reached the Rio Negro, Villegas took Neuquen in 1881 and the last battle was on 18 October 1884; the chiefs surrendered in Chubut two months later.

wars.name: Uruguayan Civil War (Guerra Grande)
wars.outcome: Rosas, governor of Buenos Aires, would not recognise Rivera and sought to restore Oribe, whose forces combined with his and besieged Montevideo from 1843; Oribe was defeated in 1851 after Urquiza's uprising against Rosas and Brazil's May 1851 intervention.

certainty.note: The frontier with Indigenous land (Pampas, Patagonia, Chaco) is approximate; the Paraguayan line is sharp from 3 February 1876.
The Chilean line is fixed by the treaty of 23 July 1881; the Chaco and the Bolivian Puna frontier stay soft.
The Puna de Atacama lawsuit of 1899 and the 1902 arbitration settle the northern and Chilean lines; the Chaco and Misiones frontiers are treaty lines.
